\chapter{Hay --- There Is, There Are, Same Word}
\label{ch:hay}
\hlchaptermodality{169}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say there is and there are with one form that never changes.}

Complete ES-C54-hay: produce hay una casa and hay libros, and say what hay agrees with.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[hay]{hay — \textquotedblleft{}there is,\textquotedblright{} \textquotedblleft{}there are,\textquotedblright{} same word}

\label{lesson:ES-C54-hay}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}I have eaten.\textquotedblright{} (\emph{He comido}.) You met \emph{haber} as the verb with no meaning left. It kept one more job, and this is it.
\end{quote}

\begin{sounds}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \texttt{diphthong-ai} — \emph{hay} is one syllable, rhyming with English \emph{eye}. The \emph{h} is silent, as always.
\end{itemize}
\end{sounds}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: one form, and it does not count}]
\begin{quote}
\textbf{hay} — \emph{there is}, and \emph{there are}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{\textbf{Hay} una casa.} — There is a house. \emph{\textbf{Hay} libros.} — There are books. \emph{\textbf{Hay} una casa aquí.} — There's a house here.
\end{quote}

Read those twice. One book or a hundred, \emph{hay} does not move.

\textbf{That is remarkable}, and you are now in a position to see why. Every verb form in this book has agreed with something: with the person speaking, with the thing being replaced, with the noun being described. In the impersonal \emph{se} chapter, even a sentence with nobody in it still made the verb agree with the thing — \emph{se compran libros}.

\emph{Hay} does not. It is the one common Spanish verb form that counts nothing at all, and it is a small gift: no decision to make, ever.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \textquotedblleft{}Hay una casa\textquotedblright{} then \textquotedblleft{}Hay libros\textquotedblright{} — the same word, twice
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}There is a house\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Hay una casa}}.) \textquotedblleft{}There are books\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Hay libros}} — the same word.) What does \emph{hay} agree with? (\textbf{Nothing.}) Next: what it is actually made of, and the fossil hiding in it.
\end{tcolorbox}
